title: Probing Collective and Individual Kondo Screening: Multi-Stage, Multi-Channel Kondo Effects in a $C_3$-Symmetric Four-Impurity Model
authors: Danqing Hu, Jiangfan Wang, Zixiang Hu, Yi-feng Yang
abstract: Collective screening has been proposed to underlie the basic physics of multi-impurity and lattice Kondo systems. But how to establish this picture and distinguish it from individual (local) Kondo screening remains a grand challenge. The recently developed auxiliary-bath numerical renormalization group (AUNRG) method provides a key step towards resolving this issue. Its application to the $C_3$-symmetric three-impurity Kondo (3IK) model with a shared electron bath reveals fully screened Fermi liquid ground states arising from collective screening of cluster spin degrees of freedom at small Kondo coupling $J_{\rm K}$ and individual (local) screening of local impurities at large $J_{\rm K}$. Here we design a four-impurity Kondo (4IK) model where the probe impurity couples only to the original three Kondo impurities to detect the nature of the screened states. We show that the collective and individual Kondo screenings give rise to emergent multi-stage, two-channel Kondo effect and unstable three-channel Kondo effect, respectively. This suggests a special helicity structure of the screened states and confirms the idea of collective screening in multi-impurity Kondo systems. Our work also demonstrates that the same auxiliary-bath construction can be readily extended to models with additional impurities to explore novel many-body quantum states with emergent cluster degrees of freedom.
summary: This paper investigates the nature of Kondo screening in a four-impurity Kondo model using the AUNRG technique. By coupling a probe impurity to three primary impurities, the authors successfully distinguish between collective and individual screening mechanisms. The results confirm the existence of emergent 2CK and 3CK effects, providing deeper insight into multi-impurity quantum magnetism.
main_problem: The paper addresses the fundamental challenge of distinguishing between collective (multi-impurity) and individual (local) Kondo screening mechanisms in complex multi-impurity Kondo systems.
main_result: The study demonstrates that the four-impurity model exhibits emergent multi-stage, two-channel Kondo (2CK) effects from collective screening and unstable three-channel Kondo (3CK) effects from individual screening.
method: The research utilizes the Auxiliary-Bath Numerical Renormalization Group (AUNRG) method, which is applied to analyze the complex spin interactions in the multi-impurity Kondo model.
model_or_system: The primary system is a $C_3$-symmetric four-impurity Kondo (4IK) model, which extends the previously studied three-impurity Kondo (3IK) model. The Hamiltonian involves couplings between impurity spins and a shared electron bath.
key_observables: Impurity entropy ($	ext{Simp}$), effective moment ($\mu_{	ext{eff}}$), and various spin correlation functions are used to diagnose the nature of the screened state.
important_parameters: The key parameters are the Kondo coupling strength ($J_K$) and the coupling strength involving the probe impurity ($J_H$), analyzed across different temperature regimes.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the applicability and extension of the AUNRG method to systems with additional impurities decoupled from the bath.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the 4IK model geometry and numerical phase diagrams on the $J_K$-$J_H$ plane, while other figures show the temperature evolution of observables demonstrating the emergence of specific cluster states.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the theoretical framework using the AUNRG method, applies it to the 4IK model, and then analyzes the resulting phase diagram to distinguish between the signatures of collective (2CK) and individual (3CK) screening regimes.
why_interesting: The work provides a concrete theoretical framework (AUNRG) to analyze complex many-body quantum states in correlated electron systems, offering insights into how local interactions give way to emergent collective behavior.
